what: Proposed rule conflicts with an existing security-pinned inline --body instruction
scenario_or_breakage: The new rule includes skills/design/SKILL.md and forbids every inline --body, but Step 5d still says the --body argument MUST be a fixed literal; after landing, the same skill gives contradictory instructions and leaves one live inline gh body path
suggested_fix: Rewrite Step 5d to write the fixed literal to a temp/body file and call gh issue comment --body-file, preserving the no-dynamic-material security invariant

what: The grep audit missed current inline gh --body call sites
scenario_or_breakage: The PR would land with remaining inline --body uses, including report-tokens posting markdown/JSON through argv, which is close to the original failure class; the new rule frontmatter also omits these files so edits there will not receive the reminder
suggested_fix: Migrate these call sites to --body-file and add their SKILL/script/md paths to the rule frontmatter, or add an explicit documented exemption if any caller truly must remain inline

what: The proposed post-push mktemp/write path is unguarded under set -e
scenario_or_breakage: If TMPDIR is unavailable after git push succeeds, the script can exit non-zero before emitting PUBLISH_OK=false or RECOVERY_BRANCH, leaving a pushed branch without the normal recovery contract
suggested_fix: Create the PR body file before pushing, or guard mktemp/printf failures and emit the existing structured failure output with RECOVERY_BRANCH when PUSH_DONE=true

what: The plan relies on a prompt reminder with no mechanical regression guard
scenario_or_breakage: Future scripts, Python subprocess argv, or unlisted rule paths can reintroduce inline --body while make lint remains green; the existing design-log harness only checks that pr create ran, not that --body-file was used
suggested_fix: Add a small lint/pre-commit hook or harness that rejects inline gh --body/--notes outside an allowlist, and extend the design-log-publish gh stub to assert --body-file and inspect the body-file contents
